{{Expand Portuguese|Lista de campeões da Copa Sul-Americanal|date=February 2026}}
The [[Copa Sudamericana]] is an annual [[association football]] tournament established in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/torre-sac-best.html |title=South American Competitions |website=RSSSF |access-date=28 March 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100201210855/http://www.rsssf.com/miscellaneous/torre-sac-best.html |archive-date=1 February 2010 }}</ref> The competition is organized by the South American Football Confederation, or [[CONMEBOL]], and it is contested by 56 clubs from its member association.<ref name=Sudamericana>{{cite web|url=http://conmebol.com/conmebol/activeCompetition.html?x=46&sub=8&type=1 |title=Nissan South American Cup |publisher=CONMEBOL |access-date=28 March 2010 }}</ref> From 2004 to 2008, clubs from the [[CONCACAF]] were invited to participate.<ref name=Sudamericana/> Until 2018, the final was contested over [[Two-legged match|two legs]], one at each participating club's stadium. From 2019, the format was changed, with the final being a single game played at a predetermined venue. [[Club Atlético San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] won the inaugural competition in [[2002 Copa Sudamericana finals|2002]], defeating [[Atlético Nacional]].<ref name="San Lorenzo" />

Eighteen different clubs have won the competition since its inception. [[Boca Juniors]], [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]], [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]], [[Club Athletico Paranaense|Athletico Paranaense]], [[Independiente del Valle]], and [[LDU Quito]] share the record for the most victories, winning the competition two times each. Boca Juniors is also the only club to have successfully defended their title. Teams from Argentina have won the competition the most, with eleven titles among them.

The current champion is Lanús, who defeated [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]] in the [[2025 Copa Sudamericana final|2025 final]].
